info.name: Ishaara API
info.description:
# Ishaara API

Requests, tests and saved examples for every endpoint. Full reference: `docs/API.md`.

## Quick start
1. **Import** this collection and an environment: **Ishaara - local** (a server on your machine) or **Ishaara - prod (Cloud Run)**.
2. **Select the environment.** For prod, set the secret `idToken` to a Firebase ID token (in your frontend's browser console: `await firebase.auth().currentUser.getIdToken()`; it expires after an hour). Local servers started with `AUTH_BYPASS_UID` need no token.
3. Open folder **2. Process a lecture** and run it in the **Collection Runner**: it submits `youtubeUrl`, then polls every 3 seconds until the video is `ready`. A video that is already processed returns `200` at once.
4. Run folders **3**, **4** and **5** to read the result, ask a question and see the history.
5. Folder **6. Error cases** shows every documented failure.

## Variables
| Variable | Where | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | environment | Server address (no trailing slash) |
| `idToken` | environment (secret) | Firebase ID token sent as `Authorization: Bearer ...` |
| `authBypass` | environment | `true` for a local server running with `AUTH_BYPASS_UID`; makes the two auth error tests expect 200 |
| `youtubeUrl`, `narrationLanguage` | environment | The video to process and `en` or `hi` |
| `question`, `atSeconds` | environment | Used by **Ask about a moment** |
| `videoKey` | collection (set by *Submit*) | Key of the video the other requests use. Set it yourself to use a video that is already processed. |
| `audioUrl` | collection (set by *Cues*) | First cue's public audio URL |
| `pollAttempts` | collection | Poll counter (reset automatically) |

## Good to know
- A new video costs Gemini tokens and one of the user's **10 daily videos**; each question costs one of **50 daily questions**.
- Every error is `application/problem+json`; the collection-level test checks this for any 4xx/5xx response.
- On Cloud Run use `/health`; Google answers `/healthz` itself with a 404.
- Request bodies over 16 KB are rejected with `413`.

pm.test('error response is application/problem+json with the standard fields', function () {

item.description: Liveness checks. No authentication. **On Cloud Run use `/health`:** Cloud Run reserves `/healthz` and answers it with Google's own 404 page before the request reaches the service.

request.description: Liveness check for deploy smoke tests and uptime monitors. No authentication. Works everywhere, including Cloud Run.

response.name: Healthy

exec: pm.test('200 ok (or Cloud Run reserved-path 404)', () => { if (!onCloudRun) { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('ok'); } });

item.name: 2. Process a lecture
item.description: Submit a YouTube link, then poll until the job finishes. **Run this folder in the Collection Runner** and the poll request repeats itself every 3 seconds (up to 200 times) until the video is `ready` or `failed`. Sending requests by hand works too: re-send the poll request yourself. A new video costs Gemini tokens and one of the user's 10 daily videos; a video that is already ready answers `200` instantly and costs nothing.

request.description:
Starts processing a lecture, or returns the finished result at once if the same video was already processed in the same language.

**Use case:** the student pastes a lecture link.

- `202` = queued, already processing or restarted; poll the status request.
- `200` = already `ready`, nothing to wait for.
- Saves `videoKey` (`{youtube_id}_{language}_v{pipeline_version}`) for the other requests.

Errors: `400 invalid_youtube_url`, `422 video_not_public | video_not_embeddable | video_is_live | video_too_long | invalid_request`, `429 daily_limit_reached`, `502 youtube_unavailable`.

exec: pm.test('200 means ready, 202 means not yet', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code === 200).to.eql(body.status === 'ready'));

request.description:
Returns the processing status. **Use case:** the progress bar. `stage` while processing is one of `resolving` (1%), `analyzing` (5-70%), `writing` (75-80%), `voicing` (80-98%) and `saving` (99%); `progress_percent` never goes backwards.

In the Collection Runner this request repeats itself (3 s apart, max 200 tries) until the status is `ready` or `failed`. Used by hand, it simply shows the current status.

Errors: `404 video_not_found`.

exec: // Wait between polls (not before the first one).
pm.test('200 with a status object', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('the video finished as ready', () => pm.expect(body.status, body.error_message || '').to.eql('ready'));

item.name: 3. Read the result
item.description: What the player and the notes screen use. All of these answer `409 video_not_ready` until the video is `ready`, and `404 video_not_found` for an unknown key. Run folder 2 first.

request.description:
**Use case:** the player. Load once, then at each `start_seconds` pause the video, play `audio_url` and resume on `ended`. If a cue has no `audio_url`, show or read `narration_text` instead. The list is empty if the teacher explained everything on screen.

Saves the first cue's `audio_url` as `audioUrl`.

exec: pm.test('200 with a cues array', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().cues).to.be.an('array'); });

pm.test('every cue has the documented fields', () => cues.forEach(c => ['cue_id','start_seconds','spoken_phrase','referent_kind','board_description','gap_summary','narration_text','audio_url','audio_duration_seconds','confidence'].forEach(k => pm.expect(c).to.have.property(k))));

pm.test('cue ids and times are in order', () => cues.forEach((c, i) => { pm.expect(c.cue_id).to.eql('cue-' + String(i + 1).padStart(4, '0')); if (i) pm.expect(c.start_seconds).to.be.at.least(cues[i - 1].start_seconds); }));
pm.test('referent_kind is a known kind', () => cues.forEach(c => pm.expect(c.referent_kind).to.be.oneOf(['equation','diagram','graph','code','table','text','physical_object'])));

request.description: Fetches the first cue's narration audio from its public URL (a Cloud Storage or Supabase bucket, or `/media` on a local server). No authentication: a browser `<audio>` element cannot send a token. Run **Cues (JSON)** first; use **Send and Download** to listen.

exec: pm.test('an audio URL was captured from the cues', () => pm.expect(pm.collectionVariables.get('audioUrl')).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty);
pm.test('looks like a real audio file', () => pm.expect(parseInt(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Length') || '100000', 10)).to.be.above(1000));

request.description:
A WebVTT `descriptions` track for players and assistive technology, and a plain-text fallback. One cue per narration line, never overlapping.

**Browser note:** a `<track src>` cannot send an `Authorization` header, so fetch this with the token and give the `<track>` a blob URL (see docs/API.md).

exec: const toSeconds = t => { const p = t.split(/[:.]/).map(Number); return p[0] * 3600 + p[1] * 60 + p[2] + p[3] / 1000; };

pm.test('every cue block has an id, a valid timing line and text', () => blocks.forEach(b => { const l = b.split('\n'); pm.expect(l[0]).to.not.include('-->'); pm.expect(l[1]).to.match(/^\d{2,}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{3} --> \d{2,}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{3}$/); pm.expect(l.slice(2).join('')).to.not.be.empty; }));

pm.test('cues are ordered and never overlap', () => { let last = -1; blocks.forEach(b => { const [s, e] = b.split('\n')[1].split(' --> ').map(toSeconds); pm.expect(e).to.be.above(s); pm.expect(s).to.be.at.least(last); last = e; }); });

request.description: **Use case:** accessible notes to read or download: the transcript in readable paragraphs, grouped into 5-minute sections (`##` headings under one `#` title), with each board description inlined as `**[Board, 02:42]** description`. Text from YouTube and Gemini is escaped so it cannot inject markup.

exec: pm.test('one title and 5-minute sections', () => { pm.expect(text).to.match(/^# /); pm.expect((text.match(/^# /gm) || []).length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(text).to.match(/^## \d{2}:\d{2}/m); });

item.name: 4. Ask a question
item.description: Ask about a finished video and hear the answer. Each question calls Gemini (a video clip when a time is given and the text is not enough), costs one of the user's 50 daily questions, and may take 30-90 seconds; the answer arrives as text with `answer_audio_url: null` if speech is unavailable. Edit the `question` and `atSeconds` variables to try your own.

request.description: **Use case:** "What is drawn on the board right now?". With `at_seconds`, Gemini sees the transcript and cues within 2 minutes either side; if that is not enough to describe the screen it looks at the 30-second clip around that moment. The answer is written and spoken in the language of the question (English or Hindi).

exec: pm.test('200 with an answer', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.answer_text).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; });

pm.test('referenced_seconds is an ascending list of numbers', () => { pm.expect(body.referenced_seconds).to.be.an('array'); body.referenced_seconds.forEach((s, i) => { pm.expect(s).to.be.a('number'); if (i) pm.expect(s).to.be.at.least(body.referenced_seconds[i - 1]); }); });
pm.test('answer_audio_url is a URL, or null if speech was unavailable', () => { const u = body.answer_audio_url; pm.expect(u === null || /^https?:\/\//.test(u)).to.be.true; });

request.description: **Use case:** the "my lectures" screen. Newest first; submitting a video again moves it to the top. `limit` is 1 to 100 (default 20). Each row has only the key, title and time: call the status request for a video's current state.

exec: pm.test('200 with a videos array', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().videos).to.be.an('array'); });

pm.test('rows have key, title and an ISO time', () => videos.forEach(v => { pm.expect(v.video_key).to.match(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}_(en|hi)_v\d+$/); pm.expect(v.title).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(Date.parse(v.submitted_at)).to.not.be.NaN; }));
pm.test('newest first', () => videos.forEach((v, i) => { if (i) pm.expect(Date.parse(videos[i - 1].submitted_at)).to.be.at.least(Date.parse(v.submitted_at)); }));

item.name: 6. Error cases
item.description: Each request is expected to fail in the documented way. Every error is RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail` and `code`; the collection-level test checks that for any 4xx/5xx response. Requests that need an existing video use `{{videoKey}}`, so run folder 2 (or set `videoKey` to a ready video) first.

request.description: Sends no `Authorization` header. Expected `401 invalid_token`, except against a local server that runs with `AUTH_BYPASS_UID` (set the environment variable `authBypass` to `true` there).

exec: if (pm.environment.get('authBypass') === 'true') { pm.test('auth is bypassed on this server (local development)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200)); }
